category.name: Privacy
category.description: Data protection threat modeling: consent, minimisation, retention, secondary use and cross-border transfer.

lab.title: Hospital Patient Portal
lab.summary: A patient-facing portal exposing medical records, appointments and test results.
lab.businessContext: A hospital group is launching a portal so patients can read their own records and book appointments.
lab.systemContext: A patient web app reaches a portal API, which reads an electronic health record system, a lab results feed and an analytics warehouse.

nodes.label: Analytics Warehouse
nodes.description: Copy of records used for research and reporting

architectureIssues.title: Full identifiable record copied to analytics nightly
architectureIssues.description: The entire record including diagnoses and notes replicates to an analytics environment with no de-identification and no stated purpose limitation.
architectureIssues.hint: Does reporting need names and full clinical notes?

architectureIssues.title: Appointment reminders carry clinical context to a third party
architectureIssues.description: Reminder messages route through an external SMS provider with no stated limit on what the message body may contain.
architectureIssues.hint: What does 'Your oncology appointment is Tuesday' tell the SMS vendor?

architectureIssues.title: No model for proxy or restricted access
architectureIssues.description: Nothing describes how carers, parents or patients with restricted-access flags are handled, so the portal is all-or-nothing.
architectureIssues.hint: Who else might legitimately — or illegitimately — want to read this record?

architectureIssues.title: No described logging of who read a record
architectureIssues.description: Record reads are not attributed, so inappropriate access by staff cannot be detected or investigated.
architectureIssues.hint: How would the hospital find out a clinician looked up a celebrity's notes?

architectureIssues.title: Lab results ingested with no described provenance check
architectureIssues.description: Results arrive over SFTP and are written to the record with no stated verification that they belong to the right patient.
architectureIssues.hint: What happens clinically if a result lands on the wrong record?

threats.title: Identifiable records used beyond the care purpose
threats.description: A full identifiable copy sitting in analytics invites uses the patient never consented to, and widens the blast radius of any analytics compromise to the entire clinical record.
threats.learnerExplanation: Privacy harm often comes from legitimate data in an illegitimate context.

threats.title: Staff read records with no clinical relationship
threats.description: Without attributed access logs, a curious or malicious staff member can read any patient's notes and never be detected.
threats.learnerExplanation: In healthcare the most common breach is an insider, not an intruder.

threats.title: Clinical information disclosed via SMS
threats.description: Message content reveals the nature of care to the SMS vendor and to anyone who sees the patient's lock screen.
threats.learnerExplanation: A notification is a disclosure channel.

threats.title: Misattributed lab result written to the wrong patient
threats.description: An unverified feed can attach a result to the wrong record, which is a patient-safety incident as well as a privacy one.
threats.learnerExplanation: Integrity failures in clinical systems hurt people, not just data.

threats.title: Abusive family member reads a patient's records
threats.description: With no proxy model or restricted-access handling, someone with access to the patient's device or credentials sees everything.
threats.learnerExplanation: Threat models must include the people closest to the user.

mitigations.title: De-identify before replication to analytics
mitigations.description: Strip direct identifiers and apply purpose-scoped views so analytics never holds the full identifiable record.

mitigations.title: Attributed, reviewed access logging on record reads
mitigations.description: Log who read which record and run proactive break-the-glass reviews.

mitigations.title: Content-free reminders
mitigations.description: Send 'you have an appointment' with no clinical detail and require the portal for specifics.

mitigations.title: Verified patient matching on inbound results
mitigations.description: Match on multiple identifiers and quarantine anything ambiguous for human review.

mitigations.title: Proxy and restricted-access model
mitigations.description: Support carer proxies, sealed records and per-record restrictions with explicit consent.

mitigations.title: Encrypt the lab feed in transit
mitigations.description: Already satisfied by SFTP; it does not address whether the result is matched to the right person.

mitigations.title: Stronger password policy for staff
mitigations.description: Sensible hygiene, but it does not detect a legitimate login being used to snoop.

threatMitigations.explanation: Analytics gets what it needs without holding the identifiable clinical record.
Attribution plus review is what makes inappropriate access detectable.
A message with no clinical content cannot disclose the condition.
Multi-identifier matching with quarantine stops silent misattribution.
Sealed records and explicit proxies give the patient control over who sees what.

releaseGuidance.rationale: Two critical findings sit at the heart of the design rather than at its edges. The unrestricted identifiable copy in analytics is a purpose-limitation failure that no access control on the portal can compensate for, and the absence of attributed read logging means the hospital could not detect or investigate insider snooping — historically the most common breach in healthcare. Both require changing how data moves, not adding a control at the perimeter. Regulatory exposure here is severe and the affected data is permanent and unchangeable.
suggestedConditions: De-identify records before replication to analytics, with purpose-scoped views.
Implement attributed access logging with proactive review before any patient sees the portal.
Remove clinical content from SMS reminders.
Add verified patient matching on the inbound lab feed.
Design the proxy and restricted-access model before launch, not after.
